newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU examines new beef label compromise.
newsitem.headline: EU examines new beef label compromise.

text.p: European Union farm ministers on Wednesday discussed a new beef labelling compromise crafted by the Dutch EU Presidency that would allow a member state the option of whether to apply the system on its territory.

Britain and Italy have been resisting plans, aimed at restoring consumer confidence in beef after a health scare over mad cow disease, to make it compulsory to label the origin of beef from January 2000.
"We have taken into account the special wishes of all countries concerned," a Dutch EU Presidency official said on the third day of an EU farm council.
The compromise also provides greater flexibility, notably over the time in which farmers must report information on cattle births, movements and slaughtering for recording on computer data bases.
But although Britain said the compromise was a step in the right direction, officials said it probably did not go far enough to gain the necessary unanimous agreement.

Unanimity is required because the the European Commission opposes Dutch plans to give the European Parliament only an advisory role instead of joint decision-making power over the creation of EU cattle identification and beef labelling systems.
"The compromise goes a little bit towards what we want," a British official said.
But in order to export, and assuming that a worldwide ban on British beef exports has been lifted by 2000, Britain would have to label the regional origin of its beef.
Britain is worried that such information would deter buyers of British beef and hinder trade in the EU single market.
Italy, which imports a lot of calves from eastern Europe for fattening, is concerned that labelling the origin of the beef would create an adverse reaction among Italian consumers.
